question: A 2-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department because of fever, cough, and ear pain over the past 2 days. He has had recurrent respiratory tract infections and several episodes of giardiasis and viral gastroenteritis since he was 6 months of age. Examination shows decreased breath sounds over both lung fields and bilateral purulent otorrhea. His palatine tonsils and adenoids are hypoplastic. Quantitative flow cytometry of his blood shows decreased levels of cells that express CD19, CD20, and CD21. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's condition?

options.opc: Microdeletion on the long arm of chromosome 22

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Recurrent respiratory tract infections and episodes of giardiasis and viral gastroenteritis since 6 months of age -> Immune system dysfunction -> Decreased levels of cells expressing CD19, CD20, and CD21 on quantitative flow cytometry -> Mutation in WAS gene -> 90%
CHAIN: Decreased breath sounds over both lung fields and bilateral purulent otorrhea -> Respiratory tract infection -> Immune system dysfunction -> Mutation in WAS gene -> 85%
analysis: The patient's presentation with recurrent infections, hypoplastic tonsils and adenoids, decreased levels of B cells expressing CD19, CD20, and CD21, along with the history of infections and giardiasis, is suggestive of a primary immunodeficiency disorder. The most likely cause in this scenario is a mutation in the WAS gene, which is associated with Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome characterized by immunodeficiency, eczema, and thrombocytopenia.
